title: One repository, explicit package boundaries

nodes.summary: One monorepo with separate packages as dependency boundaries
nodes.detail: Kernel, guest SDK, compiler integration and first-party plugins live in one repository, with separate Cabal packages enforcing dependency boundaries. The tree is a destination layout: create each directory/package only when real work needs it, and never add empty packages or placeholder services.

realised.evidence: PR #6 creates the first real packages (kyyn-domain, kyyn-plumbing, kyyn-microhs, guest runtime) under cabal.project; web/ is still absent, consistent with on-demand creation

nodes.summary: shared/kyyn-types: pure vocabulary compiled by both GHC and MicroHs
nodes.detail: Genuinely shared pure vocabulary (fact envelopes, diagnostics, reports, schema metadata) is one source compiled by both compilers and exercised under both; host KnowledgeBase/Root descriptors and KB schemas are not shared, and sharing types does not choose a wire codec.

realised.evidence: PR #12: 'First real shared/kyyn-types package: one pure metadata vocabulary compiled by GHC and MicroHs'

nodes.summary: Host package roles: microhs isolated, surfaces translate, kyyn composes
nodes.detail: Porcelain-interpreters may use both capability APIs but no native IO; kyyn-microhs owns compiler-specific interpreters and may be imported only by composition and native interpreters; kyyn-surfaces only translates requests and receives execution functions from the thin kyyn composition package. Constructor visibility follows package ownership (Validated in porcelain, no reverse domain dependency).

realised.evidence: kyyn-microhs from PR #6; kyyn-surfaces and host/kyyn composition first appear in PR #44 with import-boundary checks. Composition module is Kyyn.Composition, not the sketched Kyyn/Application/Compose.hs

deliveries.evidence: PR #6 creates kyyn-microhs as the isolated owner of compiler-specific interpreters with import checks; surfaces and composition packages still missing

nodes.summary: Pinned upstream MicroHs source under vendor/ for native and guest
nodes.detail: vendor/MicroHs is an explicit build input at one pinned revision used by both native integration and the bundled guest toolchain, available in a source build; it is upstream dependency management, not a compiler fork. Copy-versus-submodule left open.

realised.evidence: PR #6 vendors pinned complete upstream source; native adapter and guest compiler use the same source

nodes.summary: Public kyyn-sdk and private kyyn-runtime, neither depending on kernel
nodes.detail: Guest packages split a public pure authoring surface from private transport/execution support; neither imports the native kernel, and no speculative shared-protocol package is created.

realised.evidence: guest/kyyn-runtime from PR #6; guest/kyyn-sdk first appears in PR #33

deliveries.evidence: PR #6 creates the private guest/kyyn-runtime without kernel imports; the public kyyn-sdk follows in #33

nodes.summary: First-party plugins use the public SDK and ordinary installation
nodes.detail: Each plugins/ directory is independently consumable via the normal plugin installation path, using only the public SDK and declared host capabilities, with no privileged host imports; taps may select them like third-party plugins.

realised.evidence: PR #90 installs plugin source through the CLI; first plugins/ directories appear then (later local-file, microsoft-graph)

nodes.summary: Package-local tests, real-boundary integration tests, disposable example KBs
nodes.detail: Unit tests stay with packages; top-level integration tests exercise real boundaries; example and field-scenario KBs are templates copied into disposable repositories, never operated as live KBs inside the product checkout. Named entry points (test.sh, test-guest.sh, build-web.sh, package.sh) must fail on guest/plugin failures.

realised.evidence: tools/test-guest.sh and tests/integration from PR #6; examples/todos template with installed journey in PR #44. build-web.sh/package.sh never created (no web yet)

deliveries.evidence: PR #6 adds package-local tests, real-boundary tests/integration and test-guest.sh; disposable example KB templates follow in #44

nodes.summary: MicroHs is a vendored source copy recorded in vendor/README
nodes.detail: Chooses a vendored copy over a submodule: a complete Git source archive includes it, and revision, archive digest and notices are recorded in vendor/README.md. Native packages build within the monorepo rather than as separately packaged tarballs.

realised.evidence: PR #6 adds pinned complete upstream source copies with notices/provenance

nodes.summary: Shared modules declare their own pragmas with matching semantics
nodes.detail: Shared source carries required language pragmas in-file rather than relying on Cabal defaults, and uses only features with identical semantics under GHC and MicroHs.

realised.evidence: PR #12 introduces shared/kyyn-types compiled by both compilers

nodes.summary: Pure format decoding may live in plumbing capability helpers
nodes.detail: Pure decoders such as the Aeson metadata decoder may sit in plumbing capability helpers without granting that package native IO or compiler access.

realised.evidence: PR #12: fixed Aeson host decoder in plumbing helpers

nodes.summary: Build-only API catalogue executable lives in kyyn-microhs/app
nodes.detail: The kyyn-api-catalogue executable that generates the installed guest discovery catalogue belongs to host/kyyn-microhs/app and inspects staged runtime inputs via relative paths.

editorial.note: Also converts status line to front-matter metadata and basis statement
Drops the space-splitting CPP workaround rationale once the upstream quoting fix was adopted; the catalogue location/relative-path rule is unchanged
Layout comment: architecture/ holds field templates instead of walkthroughs (docs consolidation)
Desired-state reconciliation: removes status/date/basis and drops 'paging values' from shared vocabulary, following the whole-collection-read decision owned elsewhere

notes: This lane is quiet: one large founding layout, then small location rules added as the code needed them, each built in the same step. The spec and code have drifted in two places the ADR never caught up with. The composition module is Kyyn.Composition rather than the sketched Kyyn/Application/Compose.hs (matching the 0003.04 gap), and since seq 152 vendor/MicroHs is temporarily the owner's fork with a GC fix, against the ADR's 'not an assumed compiler fork'. The ADR also still names plugins/files, web/, tools/build-web.sh and tools/package.sh, none of which exist; that fits its 'destination layout, create on demand' wording, so I did not count it as a gap. I split Host ownership into package roles and MicroHs vendoring, and Guest and plugin ownership into guest packages and plugin parity, because each makes independent commitments. I folded the composition-package sketch and Validated visibility into 0026.03.
